newsitem.title: USA: Debt relief delay to hurt programs - Uganda official.
newsitem.headline: Debt relief delay to hurt programs - Uganda official.

text.p: Ugandan Prime Minister Kintu Musoke said Monday that any delay in the debt relief initiative by the International Monetary Fund and World Bank might require his country to slow plans for a number of programs, including universal education.
Speaking at a briefing for a small group of reporters, Musoke said Uganda had met all the requirements for the assistance and he badly hoped "it would come sooner rather than later."

World Bank and IMF officials believe the deal will be completed within a few days, but the unresolved issue is when Uganda will see the funding. Some officials have contended the country should get the assistance relatively soon and many believe that it could take place by April of next year.
The plan has come under fire from some African leaders for taking too long to be put into effect. But, Musoke refused to criticize the plan.
"For those of us who are debt-burdened, anything, however small, would be good for us, so we do not feel we can criticize," he said.

It is expected that Uganda, the first country to be provided assistance under the IMF-World Bank debt initiative for Heavily Indebted Poor Countries, has made great strides in recent years and was identified early on as a candidate for the program.

The initiative was undertaken when it became clear that repayment of loans to lending agencies, such as the World Bank and IMF, were draining some of the poorest countries of their financial vitality, making it virtually impossible to get on their feet no matter what reform efforts they made.
A number of other countries, including Bolivia, Burkina Faso and the Ivory Coast have been identified as early candidates for the program.
